## **Linde's Kladblok**

```{r}
install.packages(c("shiny", "plotly", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "countrycode"))
```

```{r}

library(shiny)
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(countrycode)

# Prepare data
map_data <- Life_Expectancy_Data %>%
  mutate(
    iso3 = countrycode(Country,
                       origin = "country.name",
                       destination = "iso3c")
  )

# Available indicators
indicators <- c(
  "Life_expectancy",
  "Infant_deaths",
  "Under_five_deaths",
  "Adult_mortality",
  "Alcohol_consumption",
  "BMI",
  "GDP_per_capita",
  "Schooling",
  "Hepatitis_B",
  "Polio",
  "Diphtheria",
  "Incidents_HIV",
  "Population_mln",
  "Thinness_ten_nineteen_years",
  "Thinness_five_nine_years",
  "Economy_status_Developed",
  "Economy_status_Developing"
)

# Shiny UI
ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Global Health Explorer"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput(
        "year",
        "Select year:",
        choices = sort(unique(map_data$Year)),
        selected = max(map_data$Year)
      ),
      selectInput(
        "indicator",
        "Select indicator:",
        choices = indicators,
        selected = "Life_expectancy"
      )

    ),

    mainPanel(
      plotlyOutput("world_map", height = "650px")

    )
  )
)

# Shiny server
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$world_map <- renderPlotly({
    plot_data <- map_data %>%
      filter(Year == as.numeric(input$year)) %>%
      filter(!is.na(iso3))
    plot_ly(
      data = plot_data,
      type = "choropleth",
      locations = ~iso3,
      z = ~.data[[input$indicator]],
      text = ~paste(
        "Country:", Country,
        "<br>Year:", Year,
        "<br>", input$indicator, ":",
        .data[[input$indicator]]
      ),
      hoverinfo = "text",
      colorscale = "Viridis",
      colorbar = list(title = input$indicator)
    ) %>%
      layout(
        title = paste(
          input$indicator,
          "in",
          input$year
        ),
        geo = list(
          showframe = FALSE,
          showcoastlines = TRUE,
          projection = list(type = "natural earth")
        )
      )
  })
}

# Run app
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```

**Opdracht dag 5 verwerken met huidige dataset:**

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(purrr)
library(magrittr)
```

```{r}
LED_nested <- Life_Expectancy_Data |> group_by(Region) |>  nest()
LED_nested

mean(pluck(LED_nested, "data", 1)$Life_expectancy)

LED_nested <- LED_nested |>
  mutate(avg_lifeExp = map_dbl(data, ~ mean(.x$Life_expectancy)))

LED_nested <- LED_nested |>
  mutate(model = map(data, ~ lm(Life_expectancy ~ Population_mln + GDP_per_capita + Year, data = .x))) #you see how pop, gdp and year relate to life expectancy in each continetn

#Let's take along more predictors
LED_nested <- LED_nested |> mutate(model_extended = map(data,
    ~ lm(
      Life_expectancy ~ Population_mln +
        GDP_per_capita +
        Year +
        Infant_deaths +
        Under_five_deaths +
        Adult_mortality +
        Alcohol_consumption +
        BMI +
        Schooling +
        Hepatitis_B +
        Polio +
        Diphtheria +
        Incidents_HIV +
        Thinness_ten_nineteen_years +
        Thinness_five_nine_years,
      data = .x
    )
  ))

LED_nested |> pluck("model_extended", 1)

LED_nested %<>%  mutate(prediction = map2(model, data, function(.lm, .data) predict(.lm, .data)))
LED_nested %<>% mutate(correlation = map2_dbl(data, prediction, function(.data, .prediction) cor(.data$Life_expectancy, .prediction)))
LED_nested

LED_nested %<>%  mutate(prediction_extended = map2(model_extended, data, function(.lm, .data) predict(.lm, .data)))
LED_nested %<>% mutate(correlation_extended = map2_dbl(data, prediction_extended, function(.data, .prediction_extended) cor(.data$Life_expectancy, .prediction_extended)))
LED_nested

```

```{r}
plot_data <- LED_nested %>%
  mutate(
    comparison = map2(
      data, prediction,
      ~ mutate(.x, predicted = .y))
  ) %>% select(Region, comparison) %>%
  unnest(comparison)

plot_data_extended <- LED_nested %>%
  mutate(
    comparison = map2(
      data, prediction_extended,
      ~ mutate(.x, predicted = .y))
  ) %>% select(Region, comparison) %>%
  unnest(comparison)

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Life_expectancy, y = predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ Region) +
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs. Predicted Life Expectancy",
    x = "Actual life expectancy",
    y = "Predicted life expectancy"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(plot_data_extended, aes(x = Life_expectancy, y = predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ Region) +
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs. Predicted Life Expectancy",
    x = "Actual life expectancy",
    y = "Predicted life expectancy"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

If we take along more predictors for life expectancy that relate to mortality, health, education and lifestyle, every region does have a correlation that nears 1 with the acutal life expectancy.

*Does life expectancy significantly differ between regions?*

```{r}
anova_model <- aov(
  Life_expectancy ~ Region,
  data = Life_Expectancy_Data)

summary(anova_model)

#Tukey does parwise comparisons
tukey_results <- TukeyHSD(anova_model)
tukey_results_df <- as.data.frame(tukey_results$Region) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("comparison") |>
  filter(`p adj` < 0.05)

plot(tukey_results)
```

```{r}
tukey_not_significant <- as.data.frame(tukey_results$Region) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("comparison") |>
  filter(`p adj` >= 0.05)

tukey_not_significant$comparison
```

**How to know which variables have more influence than others on the life expectancy:**

```{r}
LED_nested <- LED_nested |>
  mutate(standardized_coefs = map(data, ~ {
    model <- lm(
      scale(Life_expectancy) ~
        scale(Population_mln) +
        scale(GDP_per_capita) +
        scale(Year) +
        scale(Infant_deaths) +
        scale(Under_five_deaths) +
        scale(Adult_mortality) +
        scale(Alcohol_consumption) +
        scale(BMI) +
        scale(Schooling) +
        scale(Hepatitis_B) +
        scale(Polio) +
        scale(Diphtheria) +
        scale(Incidents_HIV) +
        scale(Thinness_ten_nineteen_years) +
        scale(Thinness_five_nine_years),
      data = .x
    )
    coef(model)[-1]
  }))

#Each variable is scaled to have a mean 0 and sd 1
LED_nested$standardized_coefs[[1]] 
```

This says that in the middle east, Life expectacy is most influenced by adult mortality, schooling and infant death.

Now see if across all datasets the same are important:

```{r}

variable_importance <- coef_comparison |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(
    mean_beta = mean(beta, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_abs_beta = mean(abs(beta), na.rm = TRUE),
    median_abs_beta = median(abs(beta), na.rm = TRUE),
    positive_percentage = mean(beta > 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_abs_beta))

variable_importance
```

Or, if I do want to see what is important in each region:

```{r}
variable_importance_region <- coef_comparison |>

    positive_percentage = mean(beta > 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,

variable_importance_region
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

significance_results <- LED_nested |>
  mutate(dataset = row_number()) |>
  select(Region, dataset, model_extended) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(results = map(model_extended, tidy)) |>
  select(Region, dataset, results) |>
  unnest(results) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    significant = p.value < 0.05
  ) |>
  arrange(Region, p.value)
significant_variables <- significance_results |>
  filter(p.value < 0.05)

significance_comparison <- significance_results |>
  select(Region, term, estimate, p.value) |>
  arrange(term, p.value)

significant_variables
significance_comparison
```

Lol, this makes it seem as if Alcohol consumption has a positive influence on life expectancy in Asia. Something else might be going on

```{r}
LED_nested$data[[3]] |>
  select(
    Alcohol_consumption,
    GDP_per_capita,
    Schooling,
    Life_expectancy
  ) |>
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

```

```{r}
#install.packages("car")
library(car)
vif(LED_nested$model_extended[[3]])
```

VIF sees how strongly every predictor is correlated with the other predictors. High means multicollinearity. Above 10 is high colinearity.

- Infant deaths and Under 5 deaths are very high, Polio and DPT are high, and thinness 10 and thinness 9 are moderate. All to be expected.

- Acceptable colinearity found with alcohol consumption so this is not the reason

Conclusion for now: Adult mortality is still very much contributing to the life expectancy, with the same named pvalue in Asia. Likely just chose it to be slightly more signficant.

**Day 7 assignment on our data**

Lets try something

```{r}
ggplot(Life_Expectancy_Data) + geom_point(mapping = aes(Life_expectancy, Schooling, colour = Region)) 

```

Here we have many values per country. If we want to see how much influence the variables have on life expectancy, let's try taking the mean per country over all years.

```{r}
#What I want to do: (1) For every column of interest I want to calculate the mean per unique country. (2) Put each value in new dataset with means and country names only. 

country_means <- Life_Expectancy_Data %>%
  group_by(Country, Region) %>%
  summarise(
    across(2:19, ~ mean(.x),
    .groups = "drop")

```

```{r}
ggplot(country_means) + geom_point(mapping = aes(Life_expectancy, Schooling, colour = Economy_status_Developing)) 
ggplot(country_means) + geom_point(mapping = aes(Life_expectancy, Schooling, colour = Region)) 
```

Okay, so plotting works. Now see which variables are strongest in correlation with life expectancy.

```{r}
correlations <- country_means %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")

# Extract correlations with life expectancy
life_correlations <- correlations[, "Life_expectancy"]

# Sort from strongest to weakest
life_correlations <- sort(
  life_correlations,
  decreasing = TRUE
)
life_correlations

correlation_ranking <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(life_correlations),
  Correlation = as.numeric(life_correlations)
) %>%
  filter(Variable != "Life.expectancy") %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(Correlation)))

```

```{r}
#Lets try plotting

ggplot(correlation_ranking,
       aes(x = reorder(Variable, Correlation),
           y = Correlation)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation of variables with life expectancy",
    x = "Variable",
    y = "Pearson correlation coefficient"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Try to add significance:

```{r}

correlation_by_region <- country_means %>%
  group_by(Region) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    
    variables <- .x %>%
      select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
      names() %>%
      setdiff("Life_expectancy")
    
    bind_rows(lapply(variables, function(v) {
      
      pair <- .x %>%
        select(all_of(c(v, "Life_expectancy"))) %>%
        drop_na()
      
      # Check that the correlation can be calculated
      if (nrow(pair) < 3 ||
          sd(pair[[v]]) == 0 ||
          sd(pair$Life_expectancy) == 0) {
        
        return(tibble(
          Variable = v,
          Correlation = NA_real_,
          p_value = NA_real_,
          n = nrow(pair)
        ))
      }
      
      test <- cor.test(
        pair[[v]],
        pair$Life_expectancy,
        method = "pearson"
      )
      
      tibble(
        Variable = v,
        Correlation = unname(test$estimate),
        p_value = test$p.value,
        n = nrow(pair)
      )
    }))
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    Significance = case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p_value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  )

ggplot(correlation_by_region,
       aes(x = reorder(Variable, Correlation),
           y = Correlation,
           fill = Region)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      y = Correlation + ifelse(Correlation >= 0, 0.04, -0.04),
      label = Significance
    ),
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ Region) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation of variables with life expectancy",
    subtitle = "Statistical significance of Pearson correlations",
    x = "Variable",
    y = "Pearson correlation coefficient"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

correlation_by_region %>%
  arrange(Region, p_value) %>%
  select(Region, Variable, Correlation, p_value, n, Significance)
```

Lets add BH correction

```{r}
correlation_by_region <- correlation_by_region %>%
  group_by(Region) %>%
  mutate(
    adjusted_p = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    Significance_adjusted = case_when(
      adjusted_p < 0.001 ~ "***",
      adjusted_p < 0.01  ~ "**",
      adjusted_p < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

plot_country_sig <- ggplot(correlation_by_region,
       aes(x = reorder(Variable, Correlation),
           y = Correlation,
           fill = Region)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      y = Correlation + ifelse(Correlation >= 0, 0.04, -0.04),
      label = Significance_adjusted
    ),
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ Region) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation of variables with life expectancy",
    subtitle = "Statistical significance of Pearson correlations",
    x = "Variable",
    y = "Pearson correlation coefficient"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

correlation_by_region %>%
  arrange(Region, p_value) %>%
  select(Region, Variable, Correlation, p_value, n, Significance_adjusted)
```

We want to know what factors might influence the differences in life expectancy between developed and developing

```{r}
comparison <- correlation_by_economy %>%
  select(Variable, Economy_status_Developed, Correlation) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Economy_status_Developed,
    values_from = Correlation,
    names_prefix = "Group_"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Developing = Group_0,
    Developed = Group_1
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Correlation_difference = Developed - Developing
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(Correlation_difference)))

comparison #shows the diffeerenced in developing and developed


```
